idiom_name: Rails ActionView partials, collections and layout with content_for/yield
implementation_notes: ActionView ships the pattern: a file whose name starts with _ is a partial rendered with render partial: "product_row", locals: { product: p }, a collection renders one fragment per element (render partial: "product_row", collection: @products, as: :product, or render @products), and the layout is the composite shell where <%= yield %> is the main region while yield :sidebar / content_for :sidebar fill named sections. A partial can even take its own layout: for a per-row wrapper. locals: are the fragment's parameters; controller instance variables leak in implicitly, which is exactly what makes older partials hard to reuse.
code_sketch:
<%# app/views/layouts/application.html.erb %>
<%= render partial: "shared/nav" %>
<%= yield %>
<%# app/views/products/index.html.erb %>
    <%= render partial: "product_row", collection: @products, as: :product %>
pitfalls: Partials inherit controller instance variables and assigns implicitly; without locals: the fragment's real inputs are invisible and reuse across controllers breaks - strict locals (Rails 7.1+ <%# locals: (product:) %>) turn missing arguments into a load-time error.
render partial: resolves through the view paths and raises ActionView::MissingTemplate at request time, so a renamed fragment fails in production rather than in CI.
content_for/yield sections must be rendered by the layout or they vanish silently, and a collection partial runs once per element - keep per-row work cheap or the page cost is O(rows) rendering.

variants.name: ViewComponent objects (Rails 6.1+, view_component gem)
variants.idiom_name: ViewComponent::Base subclass with a colocated template and typed initializer
variants.implementation_notes: ViewComponent replaces the partial with an object: a Ruby class holds the fragment's logic, a colocated template renders it, the initializer declares the fragment's inputs (def initialize(product:)), and pages render it as render(ProductRowComponent.new(product: p)), with slots available for regions the caller fills. This is the OO evolution of the same pattern - explicit data flow, unit-testable with render_inline, and benchmarked roughly 2.5x faster than partials - so prefer it for fragments with logic, inputs or slots, and keep plain partials for static markup.
variants.code_sketch:
class ProductRowComponent < ViewComponent::Base def initialize(product:) = @product = product end # app/components/product_row_component.html.erb ->
  • <%= @product.name %>
    • # page: <%= render(ProductRowComponent.new(product: p)) %>
pitfalls: Component templates are found by convention via view_component's paths and test helpers; a component whose template still reads controller state is a partial with extra steps.
Passing whole records into components couples fragments to the model shape - expose exactly what the fragment renders so it stays reusable.
render_inline covers the component alone but not its place in the page layout: keep one integration test for the assembled page.
